First — who we are

A ministry built on letters, prayer, and second chances

Many people in prison feel cut off from the world. A letter says the opposite: someone remembers you, someone is praying for you, and your story is not over. That is why 2overcomelife exists.

How it started

2overcomelife began with simple correspondence by mail. Letters came in from people in prison asking for prayer, encouragement, and someone to write back. Letter by letter, that mail grew into a ministry.

Today, people write by mail and, now, through this website, because some have told us the web is easier and faster. However you reach us, you will reach a real person who reads every word.

“They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony.” — Revelation 12:11

Why the name?

2overcomelife points to a simple promise: through Christ, a person can overcome their past and step into new life. Our anchor verse is Revelation 12:11, and our message to every reader is the same — your past is not your future.

What we believe

No one is too far gone. Every person carries worth, every story can turn, and prayer changes things. We are not here to judge where you have been. We are here to encourage where you are going.

— with love, from the letter table

For the ministry owner: this page is ready for your own words. Send a few sentences about how the ministry started, your photo, and anything you want visitors to know, and this section will carry your story in your voice.
Second — the work itself

Simple work, done faithfully

01

Letters that answer back

The heart of the ministry. You write, we write back — with encouragement, Scripture, and a listening heart. No form letters, no silence. Correspondence can continue for as long as it helps.

02

Prayer by name

Send a prayer request with your letter, or on its own. Requests are prayed over personally, and you can ask for prayer for yourself, your family, your case, or your future after release.

03

Encouragement for families

Families carry this journey too. Loved ones can write here to ask questions, request prayer, or pass a message of support. If you are writing on behalf of someone inside, tell us in the form below.

04

Hope for a new start

We share verses, short devotionals, and practical encouragement for life inside and for the road home — preparing the heart for release, work, family, and faith.

Common questions

            
Can an inmate write through this website?
Yes, where they have web or messaging access. Many do not, so paper mail stays open. Family and friends can also use this form on their behalf — just choose that option and include the inmate's name, number, and facility.

            
Will you write back?
Yes. Answering letters is the heart of this ministry. Include a reply email or a full facility mailing address with inmate number so the reply can reach you.

            
Is my letter private?
Letters prepared here stay on your device until you send them. Please still follow your facility's mail rules, and never send passwords, bank details, or legal documents through this form.

            
Are donations tax-deductible?
Please ask the ministry directly before giving. That depends on the ministry's nonprofit registration, and the confirmed answer will be posted in the Give section.

            
Can our church or group partner with you?
We would love to talk. Use the contact form and choose “Church or group partnership.” Help with prayer, letter writing, and supplies is always welcome.

          

        

      

    

  


  
  

    

      

        A note for the ministry owner
        
Getting your own web address

        
You asked about Wix, GoDaddy, and other options. Here is the plain version: you buy the name (the domain) once a year, and the site lives wherever it is hosted. You do not have to use the same company for both. A .org address fits a ministry best.

      

      

        
Porkbun or Cloudflare
our pick ↓
Both are known for honest, low renewal prices with no surprise add-ons at checkout. Register 2overcomelife.org there, and whoever builds your site can connect it for you in minutes.

        
Wix
easiest editing
If you want to update words and photos yourself with drag-and-drop, Wix is the friendliest option and looks professional. Its plans cost more than a simple host, so compare the yearly total, not just the first month.

        
GoDaddy
you know it already
You have used GoDaddy before, so your account and support are familiar. Watch the checkout for extra add-ons you do not need, and check the renewal price, which is often higher than the first-year price.

      

      
Before you pay anyone: confirm the exact domain price and yearly renewal, keep the login details in your own name and email, and turn on auto-renew so the name never lapses. This preview site can be moved to your chosen address once it is registered.
